title: England and Spain are international football's best teams, says Kane
subtitle: England ended Spain's 43-game unbeaten run on Sunday, and Harry Kane insisted both nations are ahead of the rest.
paragraphs: Harry Kane believes England and Spain rank as the best teams in international football at the moment following their enthralling Nations League clash.
England ended Spain's 43-game unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory at the Metropolitano, while also ensuring they would claim top spot in Group A3.
The Ballon d'Or winner gave the Three Lions the lead in the 45th minute from the penalty spot after being tripped inside the area by Pau Cubarsi.

Ezri Konsa and Ben White struck in the space of four second-half minutes to increase England's advantage, but Thomas Tuchel's side were reduced to 10 men in the 63rd minute when Elliot Anderson dragged back Lamine Yamal after Jarell Quansah lost possession.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored the resulting spot-kick before Nico Williams' 75th-minute strike threatened a nervy finish, but England, with the help of a superb double save late on from James Trafford, held on for a statement victory.
For the first time since FIFA rankings were introduced in 1992, England won a game against the number one ranked nation in a match played away from home, with this their seventh such game.

The Three Lions have also now won 10 consecutive away games in all competitions, the first time they have ever won 10 in a row on their travels in their history, and Kane acknowledged England and Spain were the teams to beat on the international stage.

"There are many great teams, but at the moment, us and Spain are consistently the best teams right now, but as always, you have to keep on proving it," the Bayern Munich star told ESPN when asked about the competition in the tournament.
"France, of course, Portugal. The Netherlands look strong. Germany will be there, as always."
Kane's goal saw him become only the second ever player to score in seven successive away appearances for England, after Tom Finney from September 1946 to May 1948.
But, more importantly, England have now won their last five matches since a 3-2 defeat against Spain at Wembley Stadium on September 26.
Sunday's defeat was Spain's first in 968 days, though Kane suggested it could have been a more comfortable scoreline for England.
"It's big," Kane said of the result. "We spoke after the World Cup about looking forward to the Nations League, to play top nations on a constant basis.
"We felt that we played well in the first game against Spain. We didn't win. We said let's win the rest of the games and make this a final here.

"We felt that we had more, that we could take the game to them and that is essentially what happened. Even when we were 1-0 up, we went for two and then after two, we went for three. We would have carried on, we would have gone for four.
"That is the mindset we are trying to create. In the end, it was as good a performance as I've been involved in."
